comments.why_zh: 现代几何管线概览
comments.quote_zh: 这是现代几何管线的概览
comments.text_zh: 屏幕空间反射更快，而且不需要额外的场景绘制，但它无法让你看到反射物体的“新角度”，也无法绕过拐角。平面反射需要一次新的场景绘制，但这其实相当有限：非平面反射需要为 cubemap 做六次场景绘制，或者干脆上完整的光线追踪。总的来说，游戏里有很多东西都需要每帧多次重新渲染场景，所以游戏引擎在这方面真的非常非常擅长。阴影、投影、透明/半透明、运动/深度模糊、间接光照、延迟光照，甚至命中测试这类事情（不过出于依赖关系和延迟原因，那是最适合卸载到 CPU 的候选）。任何对视觉保真度要求较低的东西，都会相应地调节性能：更少的像素、更简单的着色器、更低的 LOD 几何体、更低的帧率。如果模糊的反弹光每五帧才计算一次再混合，没人会注意到。光线追踪在概念上更简单，但（到目前为止）在任何给定的技巧水平下都更慢——你经常会听说它有渐进式优势，但这些同样的优势也可以通过努力从光栅化器中榨取出来，所需的努力与让光线追踪变得实用相当。这里有一篇关于现代引擎中可能见到的各个 pass 的文章：[LINK] 这是现代几何管线的概览：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Screen-space reflections are faster and require no new scene draws, but they won't show you "new angles" on reflected objects and they won't go around corners. Planar reflections require a new scene draw, but that's actually pretty modest: non-planar reflections require six scene-draws for a cubemap or full on raytracing. In general, lots of things in games require re-rendering the scene multiple times per frame, so game engines are really, really good at this. Shadows, projections, transparency / translucency, motion/depth blur, indirect lighting, deferred lighting, even things like hit testing (though for dependency + latency reasons that's a prime candidate for offloading to the CPU). Anything that requires less visual fidelity will have its performance tuned accordingly: fewer pixels, simpler shaders, lower LOD geometry, lower framerates. Nobody will notice if the fuzzy bounce lights are calculated once every five frames and blended. Ray tracing is conceptually simpler but (so far) slower at any given level of cleverness -- you'll often hear that it has asymptotic benefits, but those same benefits can be pulled out of rasterizers with effort comparable to what is required to make the raytracing practical. Here is a writeup of the passes you might expect to see in a modern engine: [LINK] Here's an overview of a modern geometry pipeline: [VIDEO]

comments.author: cubefox
comments.story_title: The Next Generation in Graphics, Part 1: Three Dimensions in Software
comments.why_zh: 被举为近期实时渲染的一项重大突破
comments.quote_zh: 虚拟化几何。它是由 Epic 的 Brian Karis 发明的。
comments.text_zh: 我认为实时渲染领域确实存在一项近期重大突破：虚拟化几何（Virtualized geometry）。[LINK] [VIDEO] 它是由 Epic 的 Brian Karis 发明的。虚拟化几何允许无上限的几何细节，同时保留传统的多边形加纹理的光栅化方式。它就像一个动态 LOD，游戏引擎根据可见性和屏幕分辨率动态调整所渲染的几何细节。基本上，最高渲染开销只取决于分辨率和帧率，而不取决于底层网格的细节程度。不过，Epic 的这套方案（名为 Nanite）目前还不适用于动画网格。所以比如游戏角色就没法用虚拟化几何。不过 Brian Karis 说这是可以解决的问题。
comments.text: I think there does in fact exist a recent major breakthrough in real time rendering: Virtualized geometry. [LINK] [VIDEO] It was invented by Brian Karis at Epic. Virtualized geometry allows for unbounded geometric detail while retaining the conventional rasterization approach with polygons and textures. It works like a dynamic LOD, where the game engine dynamically adapts the rendered geometric detail based on visibility and screen resolution. Essentially the maximum rendering cost only depends on resolution and frame rate, not on the detail of the underlying meshes. However, the solution by Epic, dubbed Nanite, does not yet work for animated meshes. So virtualized geometry is not possible e.g. for game characters. Brian Karis says this is a solvable problem though.

comments.author: dwrodri
comments.story_title: ImPlot: Interactive plotting library, ImGui style
comments.why_zh: 游戏中可视化海量数据的一个例子
comments.text_zh: 坦白说：我是个软件性能极客，正用手头能用的工具去更深入地理解硬件。我经常处理 Verilator 中 CPU 仿真器输出的大量汇编 trace。这些 trace 可能有几个 GB 大小，包含数千万条记录。我发现，在我这台 M1 MacBook Pro 上，常见的交互式 matplotlib 后端处理数千万个点时效果并不好。这不是在贬低 Matplotlib、cairo、agg 或 macOS 默认后端——它们优先考虑跨平台的“开箱即用”，而不是极致性能。但让我不爽的是，游戏领域和科学领域能可视化的数据量之间似乎存在这么大的差距[1]。5000 万和 50 亿之间差了 100 倍。如果我能把差距缩到 10 倍以内，我就乐疯了。我明白这个差距的存在有很多原因，很乐意在这条评论的回复里听大家详细说说。1: [VIDEO]
comments.text: Full disclosure: I'm a software performance nerd who is building a deeper understanding of hardware using whatever tools are I work with a lot of assembly traces emitted from CPU sims in Verilator. These traces can be several gigabytes in size, with tens of millions of entries. I've found the typical interactive matplotlib backends to not work the best with tens of millions of points on my M1 Macbook Pro. This is no slight against Matplotlib, or cairo, or agg, or the default macOS backend—they prioritize cross-platform "It Just Works" support over extreme performance. But it does irk me that there seems to be such a gap between the amount of data we can visualize in the gaming domain in comparison to the scientific domain[1]. The difference between 50 million and 5 billion is 100X. I'd be ecstatic if I could get within 10X difference. I understand that this gap exists for lots of reasons, of which I'd be happy to hear in detail in the replies to this comment. 1: [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 你说的那个 SIGGRAPH 演讲应该是：“A Deep Dive into Nanite Virtualized Geometry”（[VIDEO]）。另外还有一个简短的高层介绍（2.5 分钟），我觉得还不错：“What is virtualized micropolygon geometry? An explainer on Nanite”（[LINK]）
comments.text: I think the SIGGRAPH talk you referred to is: "A Deep Dive into Nanite Virtualized Geometry" ( [VIDEO] ) There's also this short high-level intro (2.5 min) that I thought was decent: "What is virtualized micropolygon geometry? An explainer on Nanite" ( [LINK] )

comments.author: raphlinus
comments.story_title: Learning Assembly for Fun, Performance and Profit
comments.why_zh: Nanite 团队将着色器输出优化到周期级别
comments.quote_zh: 他们描述说，微三角形软件渲染器的核心是用 HLSL 写的，但会分析汇编输出
comments.text_zh: 所以我会说，GPU 汇编技能在 GPU 性能工作的精英层级中是很抢手的。不一定是要写很多（不过参见 [1] 的一个例子，这是 Nvidia 的 Onesweep 实现中使用的 multisplit 内核），但肯定要能读懂它，这样你才能理解编译后的代码实际在做什么。我还会引用 Nanite 工程师们的出色工作作为证据。他们描述说，微三角形软件渲染器的核心是用 HLSL 写的，但会分析汇编输出，把优化做到周期级别，正如他们在“deep dive into Nanite virtualized geometry”演讲中所述（时间戳指向指令级微优化的引用处）。[1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: So I would say skill at GPU assembly is in-demand for the elite tier of GPU performance work. Not necessarily writing much of it (though see [1] for an example, this is the kernel of multisplit as used in Nvidia's Onesweep implementation), but definitely in being able to read it so you can understand what the compiled code is actually doing. I'll also cite as evidence of that the incredible work of the engineers on Nanite. They describe writing the core of the microtriangle software renderer in HLSL but analyzing the assembler output to optimize down to the cycle level, as described in their "deep dive into Nanite virtualized geometry" talk (timestamp points to the reference to instruction-level micro-optimization). [1]: [LINK] [2]: [VIDEO]
